probe: Can the O(K) ambiguous-terminal state from r266 be collapsed below O(K) while preserving exact duplicate safety and no silent loss of useful effects?
tested_scope: One bounded documentation-level architectural/information-theoretic test using frozen CLEAN authority, own role-local LATEST/r266 state, two public official technical sources, and direct reasoning only. No O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected authority, external effect, hosted compute/storage, paid/trial API consumption, manual execution, scheduler mutation, same-run wait/poll/backoff/retry, or optional second leaf.

public_sources.observation: AWS documents that transactional outbox can still produce duplicate downstream messages and recommends idempotent consumers that track processed messages.
Stripe documents finite idempotent-replay windows: 24 hours for API v1 and 30 days for API v2, so ordinary provider idempotency does not by itself provide indefinite retry-horizon evidence.

reasoning.lower_bound: For K independently ambiguous effects, each effect has at least two semantically distinct terminal possibilities relevant to exact recovery (useful effect occurred vs did not occur). There are 2^K distinguishable joint states. Any exact recovery representation that cannot query an independent authoritative terminal source therefore needs at least log2(2^K)=K bits in the worst case. This rules out o(K) persistent ambiguity metadata for arbitrary mixed outcomes.
reasoning.authoritative_effect_readback: A durable sink membership/readback API can reduce role-local ambiguity state to O(1) frontier metadata if each effect identity is recomputable and the sink retains authoritative terminal evidence across the full retry horizon. The information is not eliminated; it is stored in the sink. This remains Phase-1-valid only when the sink is already-authorized lightweight transport, requires no richer-mode/protected/manual executor, has no finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency, adds zero incremental cost, and survives cross-invocation rate limits.
reasoning.deterministic_content_addressed_identity: Deriving an effect identity from the durable frontier removes the need to persist K arbitrary request IDs locally, but exact useful completion still requires K-way terminal distinguishability somewhere unless outcomes are correlated. Content addressing compresses identity description, not independent terminal information.
reasoning.two_bit_success_burn: A success/burn terminal code is still Theta(K) for K independent ambiguities. Burn preserves duplicate safety but can silently lose a useful effect when an ambiguous attempt actually failed, so burn alone fails useful-outcome parity.
reasoning.closed_epoch_abandonment: An epoch can collapse to O(1) only after a proof that every member is committed, impossible, or otherwise semantically equivalent under the objective. Closing an epoch without such proof erases mixed terminal information and can cause either duplicate acceptance or silent loss.

authoritative_sink_readback_plus_determi.conflict_duplication_risk: low if sink membership is authoritative and identity is stable
authoritative_sink_readback_plus_determi.quota_fragility: must be zero optional monthly/trial/paid quota; finite provider idempotency windows alone fail

two_bit_success_burn.conflict_duplication_risk: low duplicate risk but high silent-loss risk

phase1_constraints.candidate_phase1_acceptance: CONDITIONAL_TRANSVERSAL_PATTERN_ONLY: deterministic identity plus authoritative durable readback may compress role-local state, but arbitrary independent terminal information cannot be eliminated below Omega(K) system-wide without stronger correlation assumptions.
